anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
Funds managed or advised by Advent International, L.P. (**Advent**) propose to acquire 100% of the issued share capital in NZCR Group Holdings Limited (**NZCR Group**) from Waterman NZCR LP and NZCR Nominee Limited. The Acquisition will be made through Trident NZ BidCo Limited (**Trident**), a special purpose vehicle established by Advent on behalf of its managed or controlled funds and affiliates and / or designated affiliates, entities, or co-investors (the **Acquisition**).

As part of the Acquisition, Advent has offered Waterman NZCR LP and certain beneficial shareholders of NZCR Group who are still active in the business an opportunity to roll over a portion of their shares in NZCR Group into shares in a newly incorporated New Zealand vehicle, Trident NZ TopCo Limited (**TopCo**), which will be majority owned and controlled by Advent. Advent has also offered select members of management the opportunity to reinvest, on completion, a portion of the cash proceeds or bonus amounts that they receive in connection with the Acquisition to acquire shares in TopCo.

Advent is a global private equity investment firm based in Boston, Massachusetts and registered as an investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission. Advent is focused on equity stakes and the management of investment funds in five core sectors, including business and financial services, consumer, healthcare, industrial and technology.

NZCR Group is a New Zealand based company. It is a physician-led clinical trials and medical research organisation that partners with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to design and conduct early- to late-phase trials for new medicines across New Zealand and Australia. Its Australian business operations are undertaken by CMAX Clinical Research Pty Ltd (**CMAX**), which focuses on early-phase trials, along with its subsidiary Fusion Clinical Research Pty Ltd (**Fusion**), which focuses on synergistic later-phase clinical trials.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application and on public
information available, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is
unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Advent and NZCR
Group in the supply of clinical trial services in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects post-acquisition.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
